findings.title: Push-mode pump flags quiet past their 30/60 min on-change limit publish Input Problem on a healthy pump
findings.claim: With the six pump-flag inputs configured as report-on-change sources that legitimately hold their value for 255 min, one real coordinator cycle publishes all six in stale_inputs and turns the Input Problem binary sensor on; the same flags changed 10 min ago, or re-reported 1 min ago, publish none.
findings.mechanism: INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES keeps the polling limit (30 min defrost/online/backup/booster/capacity-limited, 60 min fault) for the pump flags, on the barrier's disposition 'fails safe'. That reason covers the control consequence (a stale flag demotes to None). It does not cover the reader's other consequence: InputHealth.stale_keys feeds payload stale_inputs, and InputHealthBinarySensor.is_on reads it. const.py's own comment says the reference integration's MQTT push mode 'does not poll at all -- it pushes on change', and a defrost flag 'off' through a mild day or an online flag 'on' for days is the legitimate quiet interval the class names. The barrier census only drives each key at limit+1 and checks the reader's stale flag against the named list. It never reads what a named-equal key publishes.

evidence.contention_note: shared compute box, other finder seats running; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[k] = inf for the six flag keys (harness --perturb inf, in memory)

findings.metric_definition: Count of the six pump-flag keys in the real payload's stale_inputs after one cycle with each flag an on-change source held 255 min; plus InputHealthBinarySensor.is_on.
findings.phenomenon_property: No reading of a report-on-change source is published as stale, in stale_inputs, input_problems or the Input Problem sensor, for a quiet interval its source legitimately holds. Where a key keeps a finite on-change limit because staleness is the safe control direction, that limit must not also raise the user-facing problem flag, or the problem must be withheld for on-change sources.

findings.title: _current_weather books forecast row 0's wind as current at any age; the N-no-expiry barrier cannot see an index-0 read
findings.claim: During a weather-fetch outage of 1 to 72 h, HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._current_weather returns the wind of the held forecast's first row, not the row covering now (or none past the horizon), at all 72 of 72 hours. At 30 h the diagnosis record books 10.0 m/s where the covering row says 40.0. The fixed sibling forecast_outdoor_now, over the same rows, mismatches at 0 of 72 hours.
findings.mechanism: _current_weather reads self._weather_forecast[0] with no timestamp match and no end bound. The forecast is kept verbatim when a fetch fails or returns empty: _fetch_weather keeps the previous list and only marks _weather_stale_since, and no learner freezes on that. So once the source stops updating, the row booked as 'now' drifts back by the outage length. It feeds the house and lower-floor loss replay (_replay_interval -> _replay_step's weather argument) and the #52 diagnosis capture's planned.wind_speed. forecast_outdoor_now's own docstring names this exact assumption as wrong ('Assuming entry 0 is the current hour ... a stale forecast ... reads hours out of phase'), and #2229 fixed that sibling with _covering_index. The class barrier, tests/entities.py's _r10_covering_lookups, counts only the AST shape `bisect_right(...) - 1`, so a lookup that indexes [0] or walks a loop is invisible to it.

evidence.unit: outage hours (of 72) at which _current_weather's wind is not the covering row's
evidence.contention_note: shared compute box; count is contention-immune

perturbation.change: swap _current_weather in memory for the same body indexed by coordinator._covering_index over the rows' own timestamps (harness --perturb covering)

findings.metric_definition: Hours H in 1..72 after the last good hourly fetch at which _current_weather()[0] differs from the wind of the row _covering_index picks at now (0 when none covers).
findings.phenomenon_property: Every read of a time-indexed series as 'the value now' selects the row covering now with an end bound, and yields nothing past it. A positional read such as entry [0] or [-1], or a loop that falls through to the last row, is a covering lookup too and goes through _covering_index.

findings.title: N-log-flood barrier counts only _LOGGER.warning/.error: an unlatched per-cycle .exception or .critical passes it
findings.claim: An unlatched per-cycle _LOGGER.exception or _LOGGER.critical site (or a _LOGGER.log(level, ...) call, or a logger alias) planted in coordinator.py moves tests/entities.py's _r10_unlatched_logs count by 0, where the same site as _LOGGER.warning moves it by 1; widening the barrier's one attribute test makes exception and critical count 1.
findings.mechanism: _r10_unlatched_logs matches a Call only when func.attr is in ("warning", "error") and func.value unparses to exactly "_LOGGER". _LOGGER.exception logs at ERROR with a traceback (the heaviest flood shape, and the idiom of an except handler that runs every cycle), _LOGGER.critical logs above it, and _LOGGER.log(logging.WARNING, ...) or a rebinding logs the same records; none is read. The class's RCA countermeasure is that an unlatched per-cycle site off the reasoned list is refused, so the barrier does not make the class impossible, only the two spelled methods. At the baseline the package has one blind-shape site, sysid.py:1850 (_finish's fit-raised handler, once per experiment, not a per-cycle instance), so this is a reach gap with no live instance.

evidence.contention_note: shared compute box, other finder seats running; AST counts are contention-immune

findings.title: prepr.sh --self-test evals an unterminated step-1a3 block: every run prints a bash syntax error and its null pin passes through it
findings.claim: The self-test's step-1a3 extraction (sed from '# --- 1a3.' to '# --- 1b0.') now ends inside the open `if [ -n "$REUSE" ]; then ... else` that was inserted before 1b0, so the null-control arm's eval raises 1 bash syntax error on every run (the 'eval: syntax error: unexpected end of file' tail of each prepr.sh --self-test), and the pin 'step 1a3 lets a body naming this head run every step' passes on output produced after the parse failure.
findings.mechanism: bash's eval runs complete top-level commands as it parses them, so the leading 1a3 `if` executes (the refuse arm exits 1 inside it, the null arm falls past it), then the parser meets the unterminated REUSE `if` and aborts the eval; `echo FELL-THROUGH` after the eval prints regardless. The null pin keys on FELL-THROUGH alone, never on the eval's status or stderr, so it cannot tell 'the arm let the body through' from 'the eval died'. The block also carries the PREPR_RECORDER_CACHE line, so the self-test writes a stray /tmp/prepr-recpy.<pid>. The pins still pass (rc 0), so the defect is silent: the barrier's drive is no longer the code it says it drives.

evidence.unit: bash syntax errors raised by the self-test's eval of its extracted step-1a3 block (null arm); refuse_pin=1, null_pin=1, block_lines=18
evidence.contention_note: shared compute box; a parse-error count is contention-immune. The same stderr line ends the full prepr.sh --self-test run in sweep.py's N-body-lint-bounce row (rc 0) in a clean git worktree and in the walled export

findings.metric_definition: Count of 'syntax error' lines bash writes when the self-test's own blk1a3 extraction is eval'd by its early_head drive with stub arm rc 1 and rc 0.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every block a self-test extracts by line range and evals parses on its own (bash -n clean), and a fall-through pin also asserts the eval returned without a parse error.
